author: Kevin Rawlinson and agency
description:
Incident took place at the royals’ Sandringham estate country retreat in Norfolk on Monday evening

Two men have been arrested on suspicion of burglary and trespassing at the Prince and Princess of Wales’s country mansion, police have said.

Norfolk police are investigating the suspected break-in at Anmer Hall, a 10-bedroom country retreat given to William and Kate as a gift by Queen Elizabeth II after their wedding.

Continue reading...
title: Two arrested after suspected burglary at home of Prince and Princess of Wales

author: Arifa Akbar
description:
Royal Court theatre, London
Ryan Calais Cameron’s ‘true(ish)’ account of a charismatic freedom fighter’s plan to take a Zambian crew to the moon never quite lifts off

Ryan Calais Cameron has proved himself a playwright of stratospheric talent. His previous plays For Black Boys Who Have Considered Suicide When the Hue Gets Too Heavy and Retrograde both streaked their way into the West End. This new one is filled with mighty ambition but does not lift off in the same way.

It is based on what he calls a “true(ish)” story. The figure of Edward Mukuka Nkoloso (Lucian Msamati) is taken from Zambian history. A freedom fighter for the nation’s independence in the 1960s, he set up a national academy for science and trained a group of “afronauts”
title: The Royal Court’s new mission? To boldly go back to the 60s space race with The Afronauts

author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
description:
Reform UK leader says he is ‘very worried’ about ethnonationalism and he does not trust Tories over Brexit

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Nigel Farage has said he might have a “civil chat” with Rupert Lowe but ruled out a deal with Restore Britain while some of its supporters promote antisemitism and think race should be linked to nationality.

At a press conference in London, the Reform UK leader was questioned about the idea of a pact given that Restore is a rival on the hard right and has been eating into his party’s share of the vote.

Continue reading...
title: Nigel Farage rules out deal with Restore Britain unless it disavows controversial backers

author: Geoffrey Robertson
description:
Proving the ‘crime of crimes’ against an individual is notoriously difficult, but the ICJ has set a precedent for states to be found liable. Israel could be next

For the first time ever, a state has been found guilty of genocide – that “crime of crimes” – and has been ordered to compensate victims and to prosecute and punish the perpetrators. This judgment came from the international court of justice (ICJ), which has convicted Myanmar of killing and expelling many thousands of Rohingyas in Rakhine state in 2017.

The court did not change “as such” the definition of the crime, settled by the genocide convention in 1948 as requiring proof of an intention to dest
title: Why the genocide verdict against Myanmar has big implications for Israel | Geoffrey Robertson

author: Sandra Laville
description:
Decision to exempt plots up to 1.5 hectares from biodiversity net gain laws allows developers to dodge rules designed to reverse wildlife declines

An outcry is growing over the UK chancellor’s removal of most brownfield housing plots from a legal requirement for developers to measurably enhance nature.

John Healey’s decision in the budget to exempt brownfield plots of up to 1.5 hectares from biodiversity net gain (BNG) laws effectively means housing developers of inner-city, urban and surburban sites will be able to dodge rules designed to reverse steep wildlife declines while also allowing housebuilding growth. According to government data, 86% of brownfield sites currently registered are 1.5ha or under.

Continue reading...
title: Outcry grows over UK plan to exempt most brownfield sites from nature protection rules

author: Guardian community team
description:
Tell us about your favourite travel find of the year – the best tip wins £200 towards a Coolstays break

It’s often the surprise or unexpected discoveries from our travels that stick in the mind long after we’ve returned home. Perhaps it was an under-the-radar museum, a pretty mountain village, an outstanding little hotel, a hidden beach or an amazing hiking trail. We’d love to hear about your favourite travel discovery of 2026 in Europe, including the UK.

The best tip of the week, chosen by Tom Hall of Lonely Planet, wins a £200 voucher to stay at a Coolstays property – the company has more than 3,000 worldwide. The best tips will appear in the Guardian Travel section and website.

Continue reading...
title: Share a tip on your best European travel discovery of 2026

author: Rachel Hall
description:
Without reform there will soon be ‘no point’ in the public reporting crimes to the police, says victims commissioner for England and Wales

There will soon be “no point” in the public reporting crimes to the police, the victims commissioner for England and Wales has said, as she urged ministers to reform the justice system.

Claire Waxman called on Andy Burnham to put reforming the justice system at the heart of his 10-year plan for government, set to be unveiled next month, because victims were being failed “at every point”.

Continue reading...
title: Justice system failing crime victims ‘at every point’, UK ministers told

author: Bryan Armen Graham
description:
• Youngest title match in chess history starts Tuesday

  • First move at 3pm local (2pm GMT, 9am EST, 7.30pm IST)

  • Explainer: all your pre-match questions, answered

  • Preview: Gukesh vows to win title ‘all over again’

  • Sindarov interview: ‘I can’t play games just for fun’

  • Play through 22 famous world championship games

  • Bluesky Bryan at @BryanAGraham o
title: World Chess Championship 2026 Game 1: Gukesh Dommaraju v Javokhir Sindarov – live

author: Michael Savage Media editor
description:
Teletubbies, Numberblocks and Hey Duggee among 24 shows to be trialled on world’s biggest streaming service

Teletubbies, Numberblocks and Hey Duggee are among a host of the BBC’s preschool shows to be made available on Netflix, as the broadcaster battles to arrest a generational shift away from its programming.

In an unprecedented six-month trial, a dedicated CBeebies hub will be set up on the world’s biggest streaming service, with a substantial selection of 24 shows to choose from. It will include some of the BBC’s best-known titles and characters.

Continue reading...
title: BBC’s preschool shows to be made available in CBeebies hub on Netflix

author: Jacob Steinberg
description:
Midfielder is preparing to face Liverpool after leaving the club he loves and overcoming a tough start in Belgium

In April Freddie Potts was absorbing the disappointment of being substituted at half-time during West Ham’s FA Cup quarter-final defeat by Leeds. The midfielder was out of favour under Nuno Espírito Santo and could not have imagined that he would be preparing to face Liverpool in the Champions League seven months later.

It is the 23-year-old’s reward for taking the difficult decision to leave his boyhood club last summer. Potts noticed his minutes were drying up in pre-season, even though West Ham were not exactly stocked with talent after relegation, and was ready for a new challenge when Club Brugge offered about £10m to sign him.

Continue reading...
title: ‘I’m loving it at Brugge’: Freddie Potts on going from West Ham’s bench to Champions League

author: Daniel Wolfe
description:
Content creators have produced hundreds of millions of hours of video game since its launch

Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI became the largest video game release of all time last week and while it is hard to say exactly how many people are playing the game (current estimates say at least 30 million), there are plenty of other jaw-dropping data points we do know.

Data on streaming the game suggests that only two days into its release a cumulative 364.5m hours have been watched – roughly 41,000 years of content. Put another way, that translates to more than 41,000 years worth of people riffling through cash registers, hanging drywall, birding, diving or hijacking jets. That’s according to streaming data from Stream Charts, a data and analytics company that has been tracking Rockstar Game’s long-awaited title.
title: GTA VI’s jaw-dropping success: in figures

author: Anna Berrill
description:
Festive drinks are all about capturing the warmth and theatre of the season, so lean into wintry flavours such as orange and cloves, and add a bit of drama by bringing out the blowtorch

What are the best cocktails to make for a Christmas party?
Dan, by email
We’re all in favour of getting the party season started early, Dan, so now is as good a time as any to get your drinks cupboard in order. “Ultimately, Christmas cocktails are all about bringing a little warmth, nostalgia and theatre, so don’t be afraid to have fun with seasonal flavours,” says Josie Pink, author of River Cottage: Cocktails and Botanicals. The smell of orange, be it fresh or dried, is never too far away at this time of year, and one reason Pink suggests having a batch of orange liquor on hand, not least “to rustle up a margarita o
title: The secret to the perfect Christmas party cocktail

author: Ashlie Stevens
description:
Chicago’s Sun Wah BBQ started a new Turkey Day tradition for immigrants and other neighbors: allowing them to bring in their fowl and roast it in the fragrant Hong Kong-style

  • Tell us: do you have a special new year food tradition?

  • Download Feast, an app with more than 7,000 global recipes

Behind an Uptown Chicago facade of glass and green-glazed bricks, rows of mahogany-red ducks glisten.

This neighborhood is sometimes called “New Chinatown”, sometimes “Little Vietnam”. And this tidy restaurant is Sun Wah BBQ, which Eric and Lynda Cheng opened in 1987. Today, it’s also an unlikely Thanksgiving destination.
title: Turkey gets a glowup: how a Chinese BBQ spot remade the Thanksgiving bird

author: Guardian community team
description:
The digital butler, which can go shopping on behalf of users, is available in the US, UK and Canada. What do you think about it?

Meta is continuing its rollout of its Muse AI assistant, with the UK the latest country where the digital butler will be available to go shopping, book tickets and carry out negotiations on a user’s behalf.

The Facebook-owner’s app has been a hit in the US, where it is ranked first and second respectively on Google and Apple’s free app store, and has also launched in Canada. The assistant comes with a cuddly avatar as default, but users are invited to give it a name, look and a personality.

Continue reading...
title: Have you downloaded Meta’s AI assistant Muse or do you plan to?

author: Matthew Pearce
description:
Figure for May to September is far higher than previous peak of 2,985 since records began a decade ago

More than 5,200 deaths in England in 2026 were linked to summer heat, the highest provisional annual total since records began a decade ago, according to the UK Health Security Agency.

The government agency said 5,258 deaths were linked to extreme heat between May and September 2026.

Continue reading...
title: Summer heat deaths in 2026 reached record high of 5,258 in England

author: Stephen Burgen in Barcelona
description:
Exclusive: Ada Colau hopes public anger over housing will transfer into support for her Broad Front coalition in Sunday’s vote

The leader of Spain’s leftwing Broad Front coalition has called for a drastic rethink of the country’s entire housing rental system, and described the eviction of an 87-year-old woman – the spark for nationwide protests that in turn triggered Sunday’s snap general election – as “the last straw” for desperate tenants.

“We’re not interested in small changes,” Ada Colau, the former Barcelona mayor, told the Guardian in an interview. “We want to reform the entire rental sector.”

Continue reading...
title: Leftwing coalition leader calls for rental revolution as Spain heads for snap election

author: Alexandra Coghlan
description:
Royal Albert Hall, London
The Royal Philharmonic rode the bucking rhythms of the star composer’s intricate score, the highlight of an evening that also included works by Steve Reich and David Lang

If anyone tells you that classical music is dead you need just two words to refute them: Joe Hisaishi. The 75-year-old Japanese conductor, composer and pianist may be best known for his soundtracks, particularly his long association with Hayao Miyazaki’s Studio Ghibli films, but has parlayed his popular success into serious concert-hall credentials.

You can debate style and genre, but there’s no arguing with the impact of a man who can sell out the Royal Albert Hall on a Monday night in November with an evening of music by Steve Reich, David Lang and Hisaishi himself – and not a film score in sight.

Continue reading...
title: RPO/Hisaishi review – Studio Ghibli’s genius brings his concerto to a rapt London

author: Adrienne Matei
description:
A reader sent me unsolicited photos of his children, insisting I was missing out on everything. Why are other people’s reproductive choices so threatening to many of us?

Last fall, a man I had never met wrote to inform me that my fertility window was “rapidly closing” – and that I couldn’t possibly be happy.

What had prompted this unsolicited assessment was an article I had published about how fascist regimes seek to control women’s roles in society.

Continue reading...
title: I don’t have children. A stranger decided I was ruining my life

author: Maeve McClenaghan and Rachael Healy
description:
Women who spoke to internal investigation about inappropriate behaviour by Walliams still too scared to speak out

The publisher HarperCollins used a leading legal firm and a non-disclosure agreement to “cover up” David Walliams’ inappropriate behaviour towards women two years before the children’s author was unexpectedly dropped, according to former staff.

Women had complained to the company’s management for years about the author’s alleged misconduct and harassment. The concerns raised included that Walliams had an “inappropriate” sexual relationship with a woman who was an intern when he first met her, had inappropriate interactions with at least three other women connected to the company including asking two for dates, and approached a girl who appeared to be in her teens at a book signing event.

Contin
title: ‘It was a cover-up’: HarperCollins accused of using lawyers to shut down concerns about David Walliams

author: Jeff Rueter
description:
An Olimpico tops the list of season highlights, with mention for Croix Bethune’s feats and a four-player nutmeg

Surely the final strands of gold and silver confetti have been picked out of the well worn surface of Audi Field in Washington by now. The Kansas City Current might not have left any unclaimed after their hard-earned NWSL championship, after outlasting a late threat from the Washington Spirit to claim a first title at their opponent’s friendly confines.

Before the annual onslaught of transfers and off-season rumblings fully heats up, we offer a quick look back at the NWSL season that was.

Continue reading...
title: The NWSL 2026 goals, players and nutmegs we won’t forget

author: Mark Hendricks
description:
The trees have been functionally extinct in the US for nearly a century. But new techniques are creating plants resistant to the parasitic blight that almost wiped them out

Jeff White is starstruck by a tree. The farmer and environmentalist from rural Maryland has an affinity with the American chestnut but has never seen one stretch from root to sky like this one. “About how tall is it?” he asks. “Over 70ft [21 metres],” says Cassie Stark, director of science implementation for the American Chestnut Foundation (TACF).

“Just incredible,” White says, his gaze fixed upwards. “I’ve never seen one so tall and so healthy.”

‘Thompson’, above left, is an unusually tall specimen of an American chestnut, a now-rare species once ubiquitous in the US. Jeff White next to ‘Gladys’, a thriving 15-metre-tall pure American Chestnut in Virginia’s Lesesne forest
title: Their loss changed Appalachian forests for ever. Now the American chestnut is back

author: Jonathan Jones
description:
London Museum Smithfield
Why has the revamped museum divided its exhibits into nonsensical themes and shunted all the fascinating stuff downstairs? The results are baffling, unengaging and soulless

  • ‘An astonishing sight’: Oliver Wainwright reviews the building’s architecture

The Museum of London at the Barbican was the capital’s local museum, a crowded and quirky presentation of its history from the Dagenham idol to Vauxhall Pleasure Gardens. But apparently the location deterred casual visitors, and maybe it just wasn’t grand enough to reflect London’s self-conscious significance. For not since ancient Rome has a capital dominated its nation’s history and culture like London. So now we get the
title: ‘The lack of fun is as noticeable as the lack of content’: the reborn Museum of London is all piazza, no punch

author: Jason Okundaye
description:
The idea that seeing is believing is turned on its head in this documentary about the inscrutable Theranos founder, a world-class liar who may just be completely unreadable

Elizabeth Holmes doesn’t believe that she’s ever told a lie. She “knows” that she hasn’t committed any crime. And she has no reason to deceive you. While speaking, she is gazing at her interviewer, Nathan Fielder, with those enormous, blue, vacant, unsettling, unblinking eyes. She doesn’t break eye contact.

This is You Can See Everything, Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s documentary, which, at her invitation, follows Holmes and her husband, Billy Evans, at their home in San Diego in the weeks up to her surrender to custody at federal prison. Holmes is the disgraced tech ex-billionaire whose startup Theranos claimed the ability to run hundreds of comprehensive blood tests from a single pinprick of blood. This false claim posed
title: You Can See Everything in Elizabeth Holmes’s unblinking eyes. Or can you? | Jason Okundaye

author: Angela Giuffrida in Rome
description:
Late pontiff’s innermost thoughts, reflections and fears are revealed in published passages from his private diary

Pope Francis wrote in his diary of encountering the devil and said he saw the “gates of hell” when he realised how serious a clerical sexual abuse scandal was, according to excerpts published on Tuesday.

The late Argentinian pontiff’s innermost thoughts, reflections and fears have been revealed in The Private Diary of Pope Francis, a book curated by his close aide cardinal Victor Manuel Fernández and being published globally in several languages.

Continue reading...
title: Pope Francis saw ‘gates of hell’ during clerical sexual abuse scandal, diary excerpts reveal

author: Tom Garry
description:
• Too many substitutes used during win against Everton

  • They drop place to 13th but no extra points for Everton

Crystal Palace have been deducted three points in the Women’s Super League after they made substitutions in four separate windows during their 1-0 victory over Everton in September.

Palace admitted breaching the competition’s rules and an independent tribunal ordered the points deduction, but no points will be awarded to Everton. It means Palace drop from 12th to 13th, below Birmingham City on goal difference. The match will not be replayed.

Continue reading...
title: Crystal Palace docked three WSL points for extra substitution against Everton

author: David Squires
description:
Our cartoonist on a nightmare start for the Argentinian as he took charge of the Premier League’s biggest crisis club

  • Buy this cartoon | Some of David’s favourite works

  • And his latest book, Chaos in the Box: get it now

Continue reading...
title: David Squires on … Pochettino flying into a storm at Manchester United. Here we go again

author: Guardian community team
description:
We would like to hear from young people who play board games. What do you play and why do you enjoy them?

Are you a triple-scoring Scrabble addict or perhaps you’re more of a Monopoly player?

Board games have grown in popularity among younger adults in recent years, with games nights offering a welcome, screen-free social activity.

Continue reading...
title: Do you enjoy playing board games as an adult? We’d like to hear from you

author: Ali Martin at Carrara Oval, Gold Coast
description:
An evening of remarkable six-hitting that threatened to take out any low-flying Tiger Moths finished with England level in this T20 series and the spectators on the Gold Coast scratching their heads at what they had just witnessed.

Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt went on a rampage that will live as long in the memory as is possible in the shortest format as England vaporised a target of 185 with 41 balls and eight wickets to spare. Donald struck 85 from 32, Salt 58 from 30, and this newly-formed Welsh opening duo had lift-off with 151 runs.

Ali Martin’s full report to follow

Continue reading...
title: Salt and Donald vaporise target as England crush Australia in 13.1 overs to win second T20

author: Guardian staff
description:
Anthony Russell attacked Huntley with a metal bar while they were in a recycling workshop at HMP Frankland

A whole-life prisoner has admitted murdering the Soham killer Ian Huntley at a high-security jail.

Anthony Russell went on trial at Newcastle crown court on Monday, accused of killing the 52-year-old by swinging a 4kg metal bar at least six times at his head, in what the prosecution said was a “cold-blooded murder” that he planned for weeks.

Continue reading...
title: Man admits murdering Soham killer Ian Huntley at high-security jail

author: Paul MacInnes
description:
• Noel-Williams remanded in custody by police

  • Charges also include count of assault by penetration

A League Two footballer has been charged with three counts of rape and remanded in custody by Hertfordshire police.

Isiah Noel-Williams, 23, who has made seven league appearances for Barnet this season, was also charged with one count of assault by penetration, one count of engaging in sexual communication with a child and one count of supplying a class B drug.

Continue reading...
title: Barnet footballer Isiah Noel-Williams charged with three counts of rape

author: Robert Kitson
description:
Before the Nations Championship finale, picking MVPs for all-star hemisphere teams plus a global XV is far from easy

This week the world’s top 400 rugby players will be assembling in the same city. You can only hope London’s steak restaurants and cafes are braced for the simultaneous influx of an army of huge men with even larger appetites. If tall buildings start to sway in the Twickenham area, you will know the buildup to this weekend’s Nations Championship finals is intensifying.

Which begs a timely question. Mirror, mirror on the wall, who’s the most valuable of them all? With this week billed as a north v south duel – there is even a trophy on offer to the champion hemisphere – it is not a bad moment to sit down with pen and paper and play fantasy selector. Name two all-star XVs to represent north and south respectively. And which
title: The Breakdown | North v south: who makes the cut in our fantasy XVs for a hemisphere head-to-head?

author: Edward J Markey
description:
After the president’s meeting with Putin and Xi, the US must take the lead in restoring arms control agreements

Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping met last week in southern China, where Trump said they would “talk about nuclear weapons and denuclearization”.

It was the first time the leaders of the world’s three largest nuclear powers had come together to discuss the future of nuclear weapons. That discussion was long overdue.

Edward J Markey represents Massachusetts in the US Senate. He is a co-chair of the bicameral congressional nuclear weapons and arms control working group

Continue reading...
title: Trump must act now to stop a three-way nuclear arms race | Edward J Markey

author: Niki Segnit
description:
Plus five fantastic recipes, from seared tuna and potato to spicy butternut and lentil, to show how it’s done

Approach a winter salad as you would your winter wardrobe – with clever layering. With the greatest respect to Coco Chanel, and her famous rule about taking one item off when you think you’re done, in this instance I favour assembling a salad and then adding an ingredient. Unlike in baking, where departing from a recipe can have its risks, improvisation rewards the salad maker. Still, if you’re planning a winter salad, especially if it’s a main meal, you might want to use a checklist to avoid some common pitfalls.

The most egregious of these is cosy dullness. It’s all too easy to throw together some fresh winter produce and end up with a dish that’s more like a cold risotto or yesterday’s traybake. This often comes down to the combination of roasted root v
title: Crunch time: Niki Segnit’s five rules for winter salads

author: Zoe Williams
description:
By chance, I found myself committed to a debate with people whose views I share. It was an eye-opening experience

I was on a panel recently in a church – St Luke’s in Battersea, south London – about the future of the welfare state, except the other panellists booked to speak on the right of politics were unwell and couldn’t come. And so we ended up with an entirely leftwing panel (albeit different shades of the left).

Puckishly, I suggested that I would split my six minutes of allocated speaking time and do three on what the rightwing panellists would have said, had they appeared, and then three on why they are wrong. But I couldn’t get the arguments right. I know they think the current welfare bill is – between our ageing population, our Neets and our dated expectations about what a decent life looks like and whose job it is to ensure you have one – “unsustainable”. I just couldn’t summon the right mix of tough-minded realism and benign resignation to other people’s m
title: Let’s hear it for the leftwing echo chamber | Zoe Williams

author: Hosted by Kai Wright , produced by Monica Espitia and Suzanne Gaber , engineered by Ivan Kuraev , executive producer Jonathan Menjivar
description:
Jensen Huang is apparently too big to fail – but what’s that mean for the rest of us? Just last week, Nvidia’s board chair told investors that the company had no intention of reinstating Huang as CEO. On Monday, they turned a full about-face. The board voted unanimously to reinstall Huang, triggering a nearly $1tn surge in the company’s stock market valuation. Donald Trump took credit, telling CNBC that he 'convinced them' to bring Huang back. But questions remain about Huang’s extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy, and about whether Nvidia exploited loopholes to export chips to Chinese AI companies. Kai Wright talks with the Guardian US’s tech editor Blake Montgomery about the many twists and turns in the Huang scandal – and why Huang embodies the 'key man risk' that threatens our whole economy

Continue readin
title: Why is scandal-plagued Jensen Huang back at Nvidia? – Stateside with Kai and Carter

author: Alyssa Mercante
description:
Given that this is the first Grand Theft Auto in 30 years with a female protagonist, you might have expected to hear from female critics. But you would have expected mostly in vain

Grand Theft Auto VI is now the biggest video game launch of all time, and is likely to become the biggest video game of all time. It’s a once-in-a-lifetime event, a phenomenon that will shape games as a medium and pop culture at large for years to come, set against the backdrop of its developers fighting for their rights at studio Rockstar Games. It has snatched sales and streaming records and become the best-reviewed game ever (pulling ahead of 1998’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time). It’s also the first GTA game with a female protagonist, who also happens to be a woman of colour. Yet very few women (and seemingly no women of colour) played and reviewed it before release.
title: Man Theft Auto – why did so few women review GTA VI, the biggest video game of the decade?

author: Matt Hughes
description:
• Fifa will make decision on qualifying procedures

  • Four 2031 hosts have been given automatic places

England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales are in the dark about whether they will be granted automatic qualification as hosts for the 2035 Women’s World Cup.

The decision on qualification procedures will be made by Fifa, with sources at the domestic Football Associations telling the Guardian they had yet to be informed of the plan after their bid was formally accepted.

Continue reading...
title: UK nations in dark over whether they will get automatic entry to 2035 Women’s World Cup

author: Guardian Staff
description:
The Guardian’s picture editors select photographs from around the world

Continue reading...
title: Fire breathers and a stranded cargo ship: photos of the day – Tuesday

author: Aaron Timms
description:
For big stars, endorsing companies like Kalshi and Polymarket is just another day in the beautiful business of being – and staying – rich

When Giannis Antetokounmpo announced he was taking an investment stake in prediction market Kalshi in February, the claim he made to accompany the announcement – “We all on Kalshi now” – sounded as absurd as the howls of outrage from sports lovers seemed universal. Nine months later, Kalshi’s grip on American fans appears murderously tight: notional monthly trading volume on the platform, the majority of which is taken up by wagers on sports, increased to nearly $100bn in October from $40bn in August, as the company gears up for yet another funding round at a rumored valuation of $65bn ahead of a potential IPO. Rival prediction market Polymarket, which relaunched in the US late last year after regulators
title: The line between sports hero and gambling shill is fast disappearing

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
Trade body techUK says regulations are causing frustration with chaotic process of ‘chasing children around the internet’

A large expansion of the social media ban for teenagers has been a chaotic process of “chasing children around the internet” and could disrupt websites that pose no risk, the head of the UK’s tech trade association has said.

TechUK said the new regulations, which are expected to be significantly broader than those first announced by Keir Starmer, were causing huge frustration across the industry, including in e-commerce, which had not previously been included in the ban.

Continue reading...
title: Under-16s social media ban could disrupt sites that pose no risk, says UK tech industry

author: Osasu Obayiuwana in Abuja
description:
French Football president faces uphill battle to win backing of continent’s decision-makers in March’s Fifa election

Philippe Diallo must be learning very quickly that the battle to wrest the Fifa presidency from Gianni Infantino takes no prisoners.

When Patrice Motsepe, the president of the Confederation of African Football (Caf), asked the presidents and general secretaries of its 54 member associations to give Infantino a standing ovation at Caf’s general assembly last weekend, Diallo, a guest at the event, had no choice but to cope with an uncomfortable moment.

Continue reading...
title: Philippe Diallo learns harsh reality of mounting global challenge to Infantino

author: Gynelle Leon
description:
It will help during winter months, but there are better solutions for really thirsty plants

The problem
With the onset of winter, the heating comes on, humidity drops and tropical plants that yearn for rainforest conditions end up in something closer to a desert. Cue crispy leaf edges. Humidifiers work, but they require buying, filling and cleaning. Misting works, but you need to remember to do it. So, a free, lazy alternative has an obvious appeal.

The hack
This hack is based on transpiration. Plants constantly release water vapour through their leaves, so huddling them together raises the humidity around them.

Continue reading...
title: Houseplant hacks: does grouping plants together increase humidity?

author: Jesse Hassenger
description:
With the British actor securing the role of James Bond, speculation has now begun over who should join him in Denis Villeneuve’s much-anticipated caper

After years of speculation, Robert Pattinson has been officially cast as James Bond for a new Amazon-produced film directed by Denis Villeneuve. There’s no release date for the project yet, though fall 2028 seems a likely target, given the release dates of all of the Pierce Brosnan and Daniel Craig installments. This leaves plenty of time left on the clock for more speculation – namely, about who will be cast as the so-called Bond Girls for this rebooted installment.

Past Bonds have usually been recognizable from earlier work, but none of them had yet reached Pattinson’s level of fame before actually playing Bond. Given that, in addition to sterling indie work for directors like David Cronenberg, C
title: Robert Pattinson is not enough: who should become the new Bond girl?

author: Leslie Felperin
description:
A livestock farmer with a sad secret in her past rallies to keep military training out of her breathtaking mountain home in Montenegro

An award-winner in Sundance, where it premiered earlier this year, this slow-burn documentary follows a middle-aged Montenegrin livestock farmer called Gara and her 13-year-old daughter Nada. The two of them eke out a hardscrabble living on Sinjajevina, a breathtaking mountain plateau on which Montenegro’s government would like to conduct training exercises for its own army as well as Nato’s. This goes down about as well as a wolf in the sheep pen with flinty Gara, who rallies her neighbours as well as the local media to fight the proposal. She displays a savviness that’s somewhat surprising, even if her fortitude and strength of conviction seem completely in character.

However, that fight against the state is just one element of a film that, through long, languid takes, reveals the women’s stately pastoral existence, one taken up above
title: To Hold a Mountain review – a spectacular setting for tough savvy woman’s fight against the government

author: Zoe Williams
description:
Chicken kievs, ‘picky bits’, strawberry and cream sandwiches: the hits have been coming for almost half a century. Now Kathryn Turner, M&S’s head of product development, has become a social media celebrity. What’s the secret ingredient?

The scenes in a Liverpool Marks & Spencer, after the release of the chain’s chocolate and cornflake cookie earlier this month, looked like brink-of-Covid panic buying crossed with a zombie apocalypse. It probably didn’t help that the baked goods hit the shelves at around the time the government started asking Britons to plan for an unnamed near-term disaster. How would we cope with a national emergency when we coped this badly with the crisis of not enough biscuits?

You could explain the M&S c
title: Cookie fever! How does Marks & Spencer knock out so many viral food sensations?

author: Peter Bradshaw
description:
Yoon Ga-eun’s film tracks the uneasy fallout after a teenage schoolgirl makes a deeply shocking announcement to her class

Korean film-maker Yoon Ga-eun creates a strange world of bewilderment, sadness and pain – but not much of love – in this involving and mysterious family drama. It seems always to be gesturing at an indefinable sense of loss, a poignant keynote struck by the recurring soundtrack piano arrangement of Bach’s Sheep May Safely Graze.

Seo Su-bin gives an excellent performance as Joo-in, a high schooler possessed of a cheeky, madcap sense of fun, like her wacky, magic-obsessed kid brother Hae-in (Lee Jae-hee). She is keen on taekwondo and often shown (in borderline-uncomfortable closeup) kissing boyfriends that she will later dump. But when classmate Su-ho (Kim Jeong-sik) asks her to sign a petition objecting to the release and local rehousing of a convicted child rapist, Joo-in refuses, on the ostensible grounds that the petition talks about the permanent
title: The World of Love review – beautifully directed and compellingly elusive family mystery

author: Oliver Bullough
description:
Gladestry primary school is predicted to have only 19 pupils within two years, while its county council is forced to make cuts year after year. But residents still believe it’s worth fighting for

The kitchen in the Alman family farmhouse is large, airy and decorated with hundreds of rosettes awarded over the decades for prize-winning dogs, sheep and cows. I grew up just up the hill, so I know this kitchen well. Apart from the video feed in the corner, showing what the cattle are up to in the barn, it hasn’t changed much since the 1980s when we’d pile in here after helping our fathers with the baling.

From the kitchen, Gladestry’s small, slate-roofed primary school, set against the steep green slope of Hergest Ridge, is clearly visible, and – it being playtime when I visited – clearly audible too. That hasn’t changed much either since the days when Joseph Alman and I were pupils at that tiny school, and our own parents looked out of that same window and heard us calling
title: ‘The numbers are very stark’: This primary school is the heart of a Welsh village. Can it be saved?

author: Oliver Bullough
description:
A disturbing account of the way Russia’s elites have reduced themselves to craven courtiers

When Vladimir Putin launched his full-scale invasion of Ukraine four and a half years ago, it was a shock, but it wasn’t a surprise. The US and the UK had been publicly warning their allies for weeks about what Russia was planning, as well as threatening the Russians with a wave of sanctions unprecedented against a major power.

Putin’s foreign policy had long relied on confusion and untruth. By saying that they knew exactly what he was up to, Britain and America were hoping first to deny him his usual ambiguity, and second to pressure the men around him into making him stop, since war would deprive them of the stolen assets they’d stashed in London’s most exclusive neighbourhoods.

Continue reading...
title: From Sovereigns to Servants by Alexandra Prokopenko review – Putin and his yes men

author: Agence France-Presse in Delhi
description:
Saurav Das was due to give talks at UK universities on protest movement but says ‘coward government’ prevented him flying

A leader of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has said he was prevented from leaving Delhi to fly to the UK to give talks on the viral group’s protests.

Saurav Das, 27, has been at the forefront of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP), which has amassed millions of social media followers since its launch in May. Das, who was due to fly out early on Tuesday, said immigration officials told him at the airport that his passport had been flagged.

Continue reading...
title: Leader of India’s Cockroach movement says he was stopped from boarding flight to UK

author: Julia Kollewe and Graeme Wearden
description:
Asia-Pacific stock markets rise after US president says he ‘convinced’ chipmaker’s board to reinstate CEO

  • Comment: Nvidia’s humiliated board should resign out of embarrassment

  • Business live – latest updates

Donald Trump made up to $15m (£11.5m) on his holdings of Nvidia stock after the US chipmaker’s share price soared on the surprise return of Jensen Huang as chief executive.

Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993, was ousted by the board after allegations that he had three affairs, including
title: Trump made up to $15m on Nvidia stock after Huang’s return

author: Adam Collins
description:
• Updates from the T20 clash at People First Stadium

  • First ball on the Gold Coast is 7.15pm local/8.15am GMT

  • Any thoughts? Get in touch with an email

The players are on the field! Coles is getting the first over on his debut. Love it. PLAY!

Some lovely colour from Ali Martin, who is covering the game for us at the ground.

Continue reading...
title: Australia v England: second men’s Twenty20 international – live

author: Ed Aarons
description:
Youngest player to appear in Premier League is struggling to establish himself on loan at the Bundesliga club

Ethan Nwaneri has one record Max Dowman can never break. It is more than four years since he became the youngest player to appear in the Premier League, with Dowman, his fellow Hale End academy graduate, older by 54 days when he made his highly anticipated debut. But after a week when Arsenal published an article dedicated to Dowman’s growing collection of milestones, Nwaneri risks becoming the club’s forgotten teenager.

Nwaneri joined Borussia Dortmund on loan in the summer and returns to the Emirates St
title: Nwaneri at risk of becoming Arsenal’s forgotten teenager on return with Dortmund

author: Miatta Mbriwa
description:
Westminster council to vote on restrictions at planned tourist venue and site of band’s final public concert

The Beatles stunned onlookers when they pitched up on the rooftop of 3 Savile Row in London in 1969 for their final public performance, but now Westminster city council is seeking to ban live music being played there ahead of plans to convert the site into a tourist attraction.

On Tuesday, councillors will vote on proposals to turn the Grade-II listed building in Mayfair into a seven-storey “cultural experience and exhibition” commemorating the history and legacy of the Fab Four.

Continue reading...
title: Proposed Beatles attraction on Savile Row faces rooftop gigs ban

author: Chantelle Nicholson
description:
Chef Chantelle Nicholson says give them another chance smashed, pickled, smothered in cheese and breadcrumbs, or as fritters

I have a confession to make: I have a sprout tattooed on my arm. It’s true. Such is my love for the small, green morsels of delight. If you don’t yet feel the love, then please give these a try – those memories of bitter, soggy and pallid balls of mush will be firmly shut in the past. So versatile are sprouts that they really do earn their place as a staple in the colder months; shredded, sauteed, roasted, fried or smashed, I urge you to find the joy!

Continue reading...
title: Think you hate sprouts? Try these five recipes

author: Eduardo Porter
description:
Oligarchs believe they’re untouchable – the blue wave offers hope that the rampant corruption of the Trump era may soon be over

One can imagine high-fives all around Nvidia’s boardroom after the board reinstated Jensen Huang to the CEO suite. The market gave the move a fat thumbs-up, boosting Nvidia’s share price by about a third. Shareholders, whose interests the board is meant to represent, are surely happy.

But like Fifa’s controversial decision to defer the one-match suspension of US forward Folarin Balogun after receiving a red card for a foul on Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Tarik Muharemović during the World Cup over the summer, Huang’s absolution might backfire.

Eduardo Porter is a journalist focused on economics and politics.
title: Trump, Nvidia and power: could we be nearing the end of tech’s Gilded Age?

author: Will Unwin
description:
Even without the charges, the Belgian maestro will be an unwelcome throwback to happier times for Enzo Maresca

As Manchester City come to terms with turbulence, one of their all-time greats has flown in to remind them of the best of times. Kevin De Bruyne will be back at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday, evoking the greatest period of Pep Guardiola’s decade in charge when they won four straight Premier League titles and the Champions League.

In Europe, things are comfortable for Enzo Maresca, with three wins from four, but they have collected a solitary point from 12 domestically recently. They are struggling to score and conceding too easily at the back, leading the Italian to experiment in his attempts to find solutions.
title: De Bruyne’s Napoli return will remind Manchester City what they are missing

author: Simon Tisdall
description:
Attacks from the Mediterranean to eastern Europe to the Baltic Sea are a rebuke to western complacency. Trump is a liability, and he must be bypassed to ensure peace

Ukraine’s spectacularly successful weekend drone attack on a spanking new Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi, more than 1,300 miles (2,200km) from Kyiv, is further proof, if it were needed, that the catastrophic full-scale war Vladimir Putin launched in 2022 is escalating and spreading uncontrollably.

The sinking follows a similar incident in the Baltic last week, which crippled a Russian cargo ship, and previous Ukrainian attacks on oil tankers and Russian navy ships and bases in the Black Sea region. Last week, Russia was blamed for a missile and drone strike on Nato member
title: The Ukraine-Russia war is escalating – and it will go global unless Europe speaks with one voice | Simon Tisdall

author: Emma Loffhagen
description:
Judge Frank Cottrell-Boyce introduces the eight titles shortlisted for the inaugural £50,000 award, by authors including Shaun Tan, Eoin Colfer and Liz Hyder

Books by the Oscar-winning artist Shaun Tan, Artemis Fowl author Eoin Colfer and Nero award-winner Liz Hyder are among the eight titles shortlisted for the first Children’s Booker prize.

The award, the Booker prize foundation’s first for children’s fiction, launched last year amid concern that children’s enjoyment of reading had fallen to its lowest level in 20 years.

Explore the shortlist for the Children’s Booker prize 2027 and, for a limited time, get all eight books for £80 at
title: First Children’s Booker prize reveals ‘Great Eight’ shortlist

author: Polly Toynbee
description:
These ancient and often grossly unfair taxes are stifling the economy and young people. It’s long past time for radical reform

When voters were asked in 2020 which tax they would cut first, council tax came out on top, and rightly so. Still, it’s taken six years for an array of Labour and Liberal Democrat MPs to call for reforms to this most grotesquely unjust tax.

Prompted by a public petition organised by the campaign Fairer Share, a Westminster Hall debate heard calls for a review into property taxes, which would lay out options for replacing council tax and stamp duty land tax. Labour MPs were among those who have signed a letter to Downing Street calling for property tax reform to be a priority in Andy Burnham’s upcoming 10-year plan<
title: Council tax and stamp duty: both are a disaster zone. Scrap them and start from scratch | Polly Toynbee

author: Patrick Butler Social policy editor
description:
Joseph Rowntree Foundation report says millions could be left unable to regularly afford everyday basics

Cuts to disability benefits are likely to increase the risks of destitution faced by young people and leave millions of people unable to regularly afford everyday basics such as food, shelter and clothing, according to new research.

Destitution is “becoming the norm” with about 3.8 million people, including 1 million children, experiencing the most extreme form of financial hardship in the UK last year, says the Joseph Rowntree Foundation.

Continue reading...
title: UK disability benefit cuts risk worsening youth destitution, research warns

author: Angela Giuffrida
description:
There is plenty of sunshine, the tourists have thinned out – and no one does a traditional Christmas like the Romans

There was a time when, during a Rome winter, I would crave the warmer months. Not any more. The combination of intense heat and overtourism has made summer poco piacevole, as Italians would say – not very pleasant. So come mid-September, when the temperature drops and the crowds thin out, our mood lifts as we reclaim the city and slip back into familiar routines. In winter, the temperature is mostly mild and there is still plenty of sunshine (we do tend to grumble if the rain and grey skies persist for a few days).

Rome is best seen on foot, and my favourite time to walk it is on a Sunday. Until earlier this year, I lived in Esquilino, a vibrant neighbourhood close to Termini train station. I’d begin with coffee at Gatsby Cafe by Piazza Vittorio before walking along Via Merulana – a tree-lined street similar t
title: Why I love Rome in winter: ‘We reclaim the city and slip back into familiar routines’

author: Guardian Staff
description:
Robert Nickelsberg has been photographing the plight of the Kashmiri people for more than 20 years – his images reveal how trauma has settled into the fabric of everyday life

Continue reading...
title: Conflict without end: grief, fear and resilience in Kashmir – in pictures

author: Phuong Le
description:
A TV shoot is beset with barking dogs, power cuts and personal animosities in Nicolás Pereda’s docufiction exploring the fight for artistic space in a world of distractions

This latest docufiction from Mexican-Canadian film-maker Nicolás Pereda finds rhythm amid chaos. The film opens with an amusing visual game of Tetris; at a busy intersection in Mexico City, the concept of designated lanes and traffic signals appears to be symbolic only. Here, driving is all about carving your own path, as crisscrossing cars squeeze their way past each other. Reminiscent of Jacques Tati’s ending to Playtime (1967), this entrancing dance of machines encapsulates Pereda’s central dilemma: the question of seizing one’s personal and artistic space amid a world of distractions.

The cacophony of honks and revving engines is accompanied by an expressionistic cello piece, played by a composer called Teresa (played by Teresita Sánchez). To some of her neighbours, however, her music is no diffe
title: Everything Else Is Noise review – a musician attempts to raise her art above the cacophony of city noise

author: Anna Tims
description:
Euro Car Parks insists my vehicle was there for more than 13 hours because its ANPR cameras missed my exit

A recent shopping trip to Morrisons cost me £100 in parking charges because its car park operator insists I never left.

I’d visited the store twice that day, once at 8am and then late that evening.

Continue reading...
title: Morrisons trip cost me £100 in parking charges

author: Phil Harrison, Hannah J Davies, Ali Catterall, Graeme Virtue and Hollie Richardson
description:
The TV chef takes her sardonic chum on a tour of her South Africa hometown. Plus: Nigella Lawson gets her teeth into the Bake Off finalists’ showstoppers. Here’s what to watch this evening

9.15pm, Channel 4
Prue Leith was born and brought up partly in Cape Town, and she has always wanted to share South Africa’s beauty with her friend Sandi Toksvig. This pleasant working holiday is the result, and it’s impossible to miss the warmth between the pair. But as they take a cable car up Table Mountain, ponder the horrors of apartheid and enjoy a barbecue, nothing feels particularly revelatory. Phil Harrison

Continue reading...
title: TV tonight: friends Prue Leith and Sandi Toksvig take a special holiday

author: Bill McGuire
description:
Fossil fuel producers are choking off progress while we reap the whirlwind of our inaction. This is what sleepwalking to disaster looks like

It’s sometimes said that we are sleepwalking into climate catastrophe. But the reality is that we are walking into it with our eyes wide open, in the full knowledge that we are dooming the lives of our children, and countless generations down the line, to hell on Earth. In the UK, summer temperatures could hit the mid-40s within decades, making extreme drought and harvest failures the norm, and leaving people camping in the streets as houses become overheated death traps. Across Europe, the fastest-heating continent on the planet, the 50C temperature record could be broken as soon as next year. Elsewhere, by 2050,
title: A year of deadly floods and fires – and yet Cop31 still collapsed. When will our leaders grasp the scale of this crisis? | Bill McGuire

author: Andrew Gregory Health editor
description:
Woman hit in eye developed glaucoma as a result, with other injuries including retinal tears

Doctors have issued a warning about eye injuries linked to the rapid rise in popularity of pickleball, after a woman in her early 50s who was hit in the eye during a game developed glaucoma.

She sustained a direct hit to her left eye while playing without eyewear protection. The woman reported immediate blurry vision, severe pain and extreme light sensitivity. After emergency treatment, she was discharged from hospital and her symptoms seemed to be resolving.

Continue reading...
title: Soaring popularity of pickleball linked to eye injuries and disease, doctors warn

author: Thomasina Miers
description:
Packed with flavour and natural goodness, spicy Mexican pipián sauce goes brilliantly with white fish, while a garlicky vegetable rice is perfect on the side

As the weather closes in, I find my cooking naturally moving towards comfort as well as goodness. I have been ill recently, and while my natural inclination is to cook food that I want to eat, our bodies are clever organisms and, as is often the case, the food we crave is often the food that our systems need. A pipián is rather like a revved-up Mexican korma, with toasted, ground pumpkin seeds adding a deliciously nutty backdrop to charred tomatoes, fruity, mild guajillo chillies and light spices. It is a wonderful thing to eat with fried fish on a cold night. The garlicky, celeriac-studded rice is the perfect accompaniment.

Continue reading...
title: Thomasina Miers’ recipe for fried fish with red pipián, and celeriac and leek rice

author: Dan Milmo Global technology editor
description:
Users can give agents tasks such as booking travel or buying presents, but glitches have been reported

Want to avoid the Christmas shopping hordes? Then let your AI agent do it. Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta is launching its Muse AI assistant in the UK and is encouraging users to let it loose on their apps – and the high street.

Muse has been a hit in the US and is ranked first and second respectively on Google and Apple’s free app store, having been downloaded millions of times.

Continue reading...
title: Meta launches Muse in UK – the AI agent that can do your Christmas shopping

author: Josh Butler
description:
Singers among 7,000 artists and creatives urging Labor to protect copyright law in face of lobbying from AI companies

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Kate Bush, Grace Jones and Sir Ian Rankin have joined 7,000 artists and creatives around the world pleading for the Australian government not to weaken copyright law, urging Labor not to “not legalise the theft of the work of the world’s creators on their soil”.

The international push, the latest in a global pushback against artificial intelligence companies and their requests to water down copyright, comes the same day a long-awaited parliamentary committee handed down a mammoth report calling for copyright reform in Australia.
title: Kate Bush and Grace Jones urge Australian government not to legalise AI ‘theft’

author: Elizabeth-Jane Burnett
description:
Creedy Valley, Devon: Three oaks in a row – one is green, one is bronze and the other is shedding its golden leaves like a shaken snow globe

Leaves fall from the oak on the brow of the hill in a flurry. There is only a slight wind, yet it is as though a snow globe has been shaken – so many leaves are animated. The process seems to take a long time. Mesmerised, I follow as they glitter to the ground.

There are oaks on either side of this one. To the right, despite its close proximity, the tree has not felt the same call to let its leaves go. Instead, it holds them close – a burnished bronze, brighter even than its neighbour’s gold. To the left, a greener tree stands on the end of the line.

Continue reading...
title: Country diary: A close watch on this autumn’s leaf fall – it’s been unpredictable | Elizabeth-Jane Burnett

author: Mark Sweney
description:
Exclusive: Gogglebox broadcaster is bigger loser than its rivals after Dove owner’s strategy shift, analysis shows

Channel 4 has suffered a blow after one of Britain’s biggest advertisers ditched almost all of its TV spending with the troubled broadcaster, in favour of a switch to online influencer marketing.

Unilever, the owner of brands including Dove soap and Hellmann’s mayonnaise, has cut down its almost £100m UK TV advertising budget, with Channel 4 the biggest victim.

Continue reading...
title: Channel 4 hit as Unilever switches from TV to influencer marketing

author: Senay Boztas in Amsterdam
description:
Awareness campaign reminds public ‘traffic is a team sport’ amid less civility and more collisions on roads

For decades the Netherlands has been famed for its proud cycling culture, with a network of 23,000 miles of bike paths used by everyone from children under eight to adults over 80.

In recent years, however, like so many countries around the world, it has seen a dramatic change in the type of vehicles using those lanes: no longer the preserve of pedal bikes, they are used by all manner of two-wheeled vehicles including electric cargo bikes, thick-tyred “fatbikes”, speed pedelecs, electric scooters and even some micro cars.

Continue reading...
title: Ebikes, screens and failing manners pose challenge for Dutch cycling culture

author: Interview by Liam Pape
description:
The character comedian AKA Lee Nelson handed May a P45 and threw golf balls at Donald Trump. He explains why the pranking’s now on ice – and which funny footballers inspired him

How did you get into comedy?
I was booted out of every class for making jokes and then I discovered, at medical school, there is such a thing as a career in comedy. I was encouraged by being able to entertain the patients and went straight from that into comedy.

Who did you admire when you were starting out?
It was always the character comedians: Sacha Baron Cohen, Ricky Gervais, Steve Coogan. On the circuit Al Murray was doing the Pub Landlord. I admired anyone doing characters who could be dropped into multiple situations. As I started doing character comedy myself, I was inspired by people who might not have known how funny they were, such as a big batch of Premier League footballers from Beckham to Gerrard to Rooney.

Simon Brodkin: Unleashe
title: Simon Brodkin: ‘Which of my pranks went badly wrong? Well, Boris Johnson became PM after the Theresa May one’

author: Tim Dowling
description:
For almost 30 years Fisher played a drunk in a string vest. Now a new generation has come to know him through his cooking videos. He talks about family secrets, cancelled shows and the correct approach to butter

Gregor Fisher’s kitchen is so tidy – it looks as if he has just finished cleaning it – that I begin to worry he has forgotten (or was possibly never apprised of) our arrangement. After he makes me a coffee and we sit at the square table, I feel obliged to raise the subject: aren’t we gonna cook something?

“I thought we’d do some brunch,” he says. He steps into his larder and returns a moment later with the makings of kedgeree, prepared and covered in clingfilm: chopped onions, minced shallots, hard-boiled eggs, halibut from a fishmonger in Largs.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Two million people tuned in to see me mash potatoes!’ Gregor Fisher on his remarkable rebirth after Rab C Nesbitt

author: Nathalie Tocci
description:
The US and Russia lack the power to impose their will on the continent – the Shenzhen summit was no Yalta 2.0

The first ever trilateral summit between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin was rich in symbolism and empty of substance. Many Europeans, filled with anxiety about the Chinese, Russian and US presidents potentially colluding, saw chilling echoes of the Yalta conference in 1945, when Joseph Stalin, Winston Churchill and Franklin D Roosevelt redrew the map of Europe.

But those – particularly in eastern Europe – who are fretting about another historic betrayal should remember that when it comes to European security today, we are the ones who hold most of the cards. Far more meaningful last week than Shenzhen was a
title: Europe’s big threat is not Trump and Putin redrawing the map. It’s our own learned helplessness | Natalie Tocci

author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
description:
South Korea has made exams a career-defining way to level the playing field, but AI has plunged the system into chaos

“I have never worn glasses in my life,” Yun Jeong-hu says to the camera, holding up a tax law textbook, and flipping through pages plastered with notes and dotted with highlighted sections.

In the 22-minute video, the 25-year-old talks viewers through his study methods, naming his tutors, describing watching recorded lectures until 3am, and solving a corporate tax question live and unrehearsed.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Produce a good result by any means’: how AI is testing South Korea’s exam obsession

author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
description:
The order was issued after aircraft entered the country’s air defence identification zone over the island of Ulleungdo

Residents of a remote South Korean island were ordered to take shelter on Tuesday morning after several Russian military aircraft came close to entering its airspace, prompting a pre-emptive alert from the military that anticipated a violation.

The defence ministry said it would summon the Russian defence attaché on Tuesday afternoon to lodge a strong protest.

Continue reading...
title: South Korea tells island residents to take shelter after Russian military aircraft approach

author: Associated Press
description:
Accused official leaked national secrets to unnamed country and received payments worth over $150,000, state-linked publisher says

A Chinese official has been sentenced to death for spying for a foreign country, a government-linked publisher has said.

Gold Wall Press, a publishing company associated with China’s national administration of state secrets protection, said the convicted person was surnamed Ma and was approached and recruited by an unnamed foreign intelligence service while working abroad.

Continue reading...
title: China sentences official to death for spying for foreign country

author: Josh Butler
description:
Individual Australians will be able to sue big tech companies for harm suffered online under compromise deal announced on Tuesday

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Big tech companies could be hit with “multi-billion dollar” fines and individuals could sue social media companies in court, under Australia’s new digital duty of care laws, with the Greens extracting major amendments from Labor.

The government’s legislation will pass parliament this week after the Greens agreed to support the bill
title: Social media companies could be fined 5% of global revenue after Labor and Greens join forces on online safety laws

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Tripoli-based foreign ministry demands explanation from Kyiv; Guardian analysis identifies more than 460,000 Russian deaths linked to the war. What we know on day 1,735

Continue reading...
title: Ukraine war briefing: Kyiv’s strike on Russian ships in Benghazi condemned by Libya’s UN-backed government

author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
description:
Position contrasts with Green party’s policies before 2024 election, as polls show just 17% of voters trust them on defence

Zack Polanski has given his backing to a paper that endorses Britain’s membership of Nato and the maintenance of the country’s nuclear weapons.

The Green party leader has welcomed a report from the Verdant thinktank that says the UK should remain in the military alliance and calls for the country to cooperate more closely with France on the maintenance of its nuclear weapons.

Continue reading...
title: Zack Polanski backs report endorsing Nato membership and maintaining nuclear weapons

author: Patrick Barkham
description:
Nature writer reveals in his first Reith lecture that he finds ‘much more hope’ in emerging alliances

We are “misplacing our trust” in the Cop climate summits and their “capacity to deliver consequential change”, according to Robert Macfarlane in this year’s Reith lectures.

In comments recorded before this week’s failure of the 31st UN climate summit to deliver an agreement on action to combat global heating, the bestselling author said he saw “much more hope” in emerging alliances such as the Santa Marta process, which is a smaller group of countries committed to phasing out fossil fuels as soon as possible.

Continue reading...
title: Robert Macfarlane says trust in Cop to deliver change on climate is ‘misplaced’

author: Oliver Wainwright
description:
After a 10-year transformation, the glorious cathedral-like Smithfields market is now telling the capital’s story. Our architecture critic enters a world of jewels, axes, DJs and dog races – with unposh coffee from Syd’s century-old stall

‘All the grit and the glitters,” trumpets a big illuminated sign on the roof of the old Smithfield general market, beaming out as if advertising a raunchy burlesque show. It is the jazzy tagline of the new-look London Museum, which has gone from being marooned on a roundabout in an armpit of the City to taking over this prime Victorian market complex, following an arduous decade-long transformation.

The slogan is fitting for a museum that displays everything from priceless Tudor jewels to a lump of congealed fat and rags dredged from a Whitechapel sewer. Just as the colossal fatberg was scraped from the mu
title: Take me to the fatberg! The £437m new Museum of London is an astonishing sight
